merger_description:
Surge AU BidCo Pty Ltd (**Surge BidCo**) proposes to acquire NOJA Power Switchgear Pty Ltd and its subsidiaries (together, **NOJA**).  

NOJA is engaged in the design, manufacture, sale and distribution of medium voltage electrical equipment and supporting software. NOJA primarily develops pole-mounted, medium-voltage, auto-reclosing circuit breakers (or ‘reclosers’). Reclosers have many applications for utilities, but are primarily installed on overhead distribution powerlines and used by utilities to protect and manage electricity distribution grids, auto-reclosing the circuit and maintaining power in circumstances of a transient fault in the grid (for example lightning strike, high winds, animal / bird interference). NOJA assembles these reclosers and its other products at its facility in Brisbane. NOJA’s Australian customers consist of electricity and utilities distribution providers in each state.  

Surge BidCo is a newly incorporated Australian company established for the purpose of acquiring the shares in the NOJA.  

Surge BidCo is, and NOJA will (post completion) be, controlled and indirectly majority owned by Goldman Sachs Asset Management Singapore Pte Ltd, which is indirectly wholly owned by The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (**Goldman Sachs**), and other affiliates of Goldman Sachs.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition, given there is no horizontal overlap or
vertical relationship between Goldman Sachs (and its connected
entities) and NOJA in Australia
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
